Load proteins from multiple assemblies

Source: R/load.R
load_proteins.Rd

Main entry point for loading protein data. Discovers and loads FASTA files, optionally with associated score and name mapping files.

Usage

load_proteins(
  fasta_dir,
  score_dir = NULL,
  pattern = "*.faa",
  name_mapping = TRUE,
  quiet = FALSE
)

Arguments

fasta_dir

Character. Directory containing FASTA files.

score_dir

Character. Optional directory containing score CSV files.

pattern

Character. Glob pattern for FASTA files (default: "*.faa"). Use e.g. "*.faa.gz" for gzipped files or "*.fa*" for mixed extensions.

name_mapping

Logical. Whether to record name mapping files.

quiet

Logical. If FALSE (default), print a one-line summary of what was loaded. Warnings are shown regardless.

Value

A protein_collection object.

File naming conventions

Each FASTA file in fasta_dir is treated as one assembly. The assembly name is the file name without its extension (and without a trailing .gz), so isolate_A.faa and isolate_A.faa.gz both give the assembly isolate_A.

Optional companion files are matched by assembly name:

  • <assembly>_scored.csv in score_dir - effector prediction scores (see below). A warning is issued for every assembly with no score file.

  • <assembly>_name_mapping.csv in fasta_dir - omnieff name mapping (recorded in source_files, not merged).

FASTA requirements

Files must contain protein (amino acid) sequences. Nucleotide input is rejected with an error. Headers are split at the first whitespace: the first token becomes protein_id and the remainder (if any) is kept in a description column. For example >XP_001 cytochrome P450 [P. oryzae] gives protein_id = "XP_001" and description = "cytochrome P450 [P. oryzae]". Protein IDs must be unique across all assemblies. Trailing stop codons (*) are removed and sequences are upper-cased.

Score file format

A score file is a CSV with one row per protein and at least these columns:

  • protein_id - must match the FASTA IDs (first header token) exactly

  • custom_score - numeric effector score used by score_threshold in build_pa_matrix() and by plot_scores()

The omnieff pipeline also writes assembly, score_rank, and many per-tool columns; all extra columns are kept. The value RESULTS_MISSING (and empty strings) are read as NA. A warning is issued if none of the IDs in a score file match the FASTA.

Examples

# Bundled example data: three assemblies with scores
data_dir <- system.file("testdata", package = "paneffectR")
proteins <- load_proteins(fasta_dir = data_dir, score_dir = data_dir)
#> ✔ Loaded 3 assemblies (300 proteins) from
#>   /home/runner/work/_temp/Library/paneffectR/testdata
#> ℹ Scores: found for 3 of 3 assemblies, matched 300 of 300 proteins
proteins
#> -- protein_collection --
#> 3 assemblies, 300 total proteins
#> Scores: present
#> 
#> # A tibble: 3 × 3
#>   assembly_name n_proteins has_scores
#>   <chr>              <int> <lgl>     
#> 1 assembly1            100 TRUE      
#> 2 assembly2            100 TRUE      
#> 3 assembly3            100 TRUE      

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Load from omnieff output
proteins <- load_proteins(
  fasta_dir = "reformatted/",
  score_dir = "scored/"
)

# Load gzipped FASTAs without scores
proteins <- load_proteins(fasta_dir = "my_fastas/", pattern = "*.faa.gz")
} # }
